title: Single cell transcriptome sequencing of the developing human embryonic meninges
corresponding_author: Sten Linnarsson (Data Access Committee) / David R Raleigh, Roger A. Barker, Oscar Persson, Erik Sundstrom (data producers/collaborators)
platform: Illumina NovaSeq 6000, 10x Genomics Chromium (S4 flow cell, target 100,000 reads/cell)
reference_genome: GRCh38.p12, ENSEMBL release 93 gene annotations (10x Genomics GRCh38-3.0.0 reference package)
patient_count: Not applicable (13 human embryonic specimens, not patients)
anatomic_location_breakdown: Whole dissected meninges for most embryos (20 of 24 samples, per EGA sample-level 'Meninges of embryo PCW X.X' descriptions); one embryo (subject_id BRC2301, 4 samples) had meninges subdivided by region: forebrain dorsal, forebrain ventral, midbrain/hindbrain dorsal, and midbrain/hindbrain ventral. Note this is fetal developmental anatomy, not the adult tumor-location vocabulary (convexity/skull_base/etc.) in docs/controlled_vocabulary.md, which does not apply to this specimen type.
sex_distribution: Not reported (EGA sample-level metadata lists biological_sex as 'unknown' for all 24 samples)
age_distribution: 13 human embryos, per-sample post-conceptional week (PCW) values ranging 5.5-13.5 (per EGA sample-level descriptions); the dataset-level description states the range as PCW 5.0-13.0, a minor discrepancy noted here rather than resolved by estimation.
processed_data_format: STARSolo-processed BAM files, 24 total (one per sample), per the EGAD50000001434 dataset description
license: Not reported (governed by a Data Access Agreement per policy EGAP50000000516, not a conventional data license)
controlled_access_approval_timeline: Requires Data Access Committee approval (DAC EGAC50000000576, chaired by Sten Linnarsson, Karolinska Institutet) via a signed Data Access Agreement (policy EGAP50000000516); specific approval turnaround time is not stated in the public metadata.
needs_manual_review_reason: NORMAL/REFERENCE TISSUE, LOGGED PER docs/scope.md's explicit rule that normal/reference tissue atlases (here, normal developing human meninges) belong in /data/adjacent/, not core, even though this is patient-adjacent basic-biology work directly motivated by meningioma cell-of-origin research (per the EGA study description: 'this dataset should help discover cells of origin for meningiomas'). CONTROLLED-ACCESS COMPLIANCE: verified only via the public EGA Metadata API (metadata.ega-archive.org/studies/EGAS50000000980, /datasets/EGAD50000001434, /datasets/EGAD50000001434/samples, /datasets/EGAD50000001434/runs, /policies/EGAP50000000516); the controlled sequencing data itself was never accessed, per docs/scope.md's instruction for controlled-access datasets. Study-level EGA metadata lists pubmed_ids as an empty array (no linked publication yet); a targeted PubMed search for a matching Linnarsson-lab or Raleigh-lab embryonic-meninges single-cell atlas paper did not surface a confirmed match as of this extraction, so publications is left empty rather than guessed; confidence_level.publications is Low to flag that this should be re-checked as new papers are indexed. Sample count (24) and unique-embryo count (13, via distinct subject_id values in the /samples endpoint) both independently corroborate the dataset title's own claim ('24 samples from 13 individual human embryonic meninges'). CONTROLLED-VOCABULARY GAP: who_edition has no enum value appropriate for normal/non-neoplastic tissue (only '2016', '2021', 'Not applicable (cell line)', or 'Not reported' exist in docs/controlled_vocabulary.md); 'Not reported' was used here as the closest available literal value rather than the cell-line-flavored 'Not applicable (cell line)', since this is neither a tumor nor a cell line; recommend docs/controlled_vocabulary.md add a 'Not applicable (normal tissue)' or similar value for future normal-tissue adjacent records. corresponding_author/institution derived from the EGA Data Access Agreement (policy EGAP50000000516), which names Sten Linnarsson as the Data Access Committee/signatory (Karolinska Institutet) and lists Roger A. Barker, Oscar Persson, David R. Raleigh, and Erik Sundstrom as other data producers/collaborators; no single 'corresponding author' is designated in the public metadata the way a GEO record designates one, so both are given here for transparency. date_deposited left 'Not reported' since the EGA API exposes only a released_date (2025-06-25, used for date_updated), not a distinct submission date. UPDATE 2026-07-13: the monthly refresh's new pan_atlas_check (cellxgene) surfaced collection 7d66d871-091f-4602-9f42-85f86d2853e0 ('Single cell RNA sequencing of the human embryonic meninges at 5-13 weeks post conception') as an apparent new candidate; verified directly against the live cellxgene Curation API and confirmed this is the same 13-embryo cohort as this record, not a separate dataset -- same institution (Karolinska), same corresponding contact (Sten Linnarsson), same specimen count and post-conceptional-week range, same research aim (meningioma cell-of-origin). Rather than write a duplicate record, cellxgene's collection id was added to related_accessions and source_urls here. This also resolves part of the earlier raw/processed-data gap: cellxgene hosts a public, open-access processed (h5ad) version of this cohort (broken out by cell type: Neural, Vascular_perivascular, Immune, Fibroblasts, Erythropoietic, Vascular_endothelial, Epithelial, Neural_crest, plus a combined All_cells object of 156,726 cells), even though the raw sequencing data remains controlled-access via EGA -- access_type/raw_data_available above still describe the EGA-hosted raw data specifically. No DOI or linked publication is exposed by the cellxgene collection either, consistent with the 'no publication yet' finding already recorded above.
